_doc: #ipc the ratchet behind cloud-android-ipc-mesh.py I3 (a0_docs/eng-specs/fleet-ipc.md). Rule: two fleet apps on the same phone talk over Android IPC (libs:devtools FleetIpc, a provider, a bound service, an intent), never over a loopback socket. Every Kotlin/Java file under a[abc]_* that holds a loopback HTTP client shape (a socket to 127.0.0.1/localhost, an http(s)/ws URL on loopback, the FleetIpcWire.httpGet rung, URL(RishBridge.bridgeUrl())) must be listed here with the most it may hold and WHY it is not an app-to-app call on the phone. A new file, or one more shape in a listed file, fails the guard; a file that drops below its count must lower it (the list only shrinks).

aa_cloud-superapp/app/src/main/java/com/.why: the gateway's own address in /api/fleet/apps, for external callers; a label

Configs > Network > Webserver: the fallback URL (localhost:8002) handed to Cloud Browser as an ACTION_VIEW intent when Cloud C3 Webserver is not installed; the app itself is opened by its explicit launch intent, and SuperApp opens no socket to it

ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/appstore/src/m.why: addresses PRINTED for external callers: the gateway's (catalogue, markdown) and a pre-gateway build's own port (catalogue base, markdown); labels, not clients
Apps Mesh's version-skew rung: the open ping of a pre-IPC member's assigned port (looking without waking), its range sweep, and StoreMesh.ask's HTTP fallback for a member with no IPC door

ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/devtools/src/m.why: calls the version-skew rung (FleetIpcWire.httpGet) when the callee has no IPC door, and names the gateway's address (gatewayBase) for external callers; a label
THE version-skew rung (httpGet): a member built before the fleet IPC layer is asked on its old loopback debug port; FleetIpc.call reaches it only when the provider call returned nothing

ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/shizuku-adb-de.why: this app's OWN app_process shell server (uid 2000, started by adb), not a fleet app
version skew only: a SuperApp from before the IPC adb/exec route is asked on its loopback DevControlServer (asked over FleetIpc first)

ac_cloud-code/src/plugins/browser/androi.why: upstream Acode: its in-app browser previews the user's own localhost dev server; no fleet app

ac_cloud-code/src/plugins/terminal/src/a.why: upstream Acode: its own terminal process server inside Cloud Code; no fleet app

ac_cloud-myterminal/hub/src/main/java/co.why: the address of MyTerminal's own opt-in dev API, shown in its own UI; a label

ac_cloud-nav/app/src/main/java/com/diego.why: the 'base' string Cloud Nav's own (opt-in) dev server prints in its /api/docs; a label

ac_cloud-vault/app/src/main/kotlin/com/x.why: upstream Bitwarden: a sample domain string in a Compose preview; not a client

ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/crash/src/main.why: #1122 the crash report's POST to the phone's OWN C3 WebServer sink (POST /__app__/api/crashes on 127.0.0.1, the port baked from ac_cloud-c3-webserver/build.json::runtime.port): a plain socket written from the crashing process, which has no time to bind a service and may be killed any moment. It is not an app-to-app call (the report is the app's own data going to the on-phone log sink, offline-safe, no DNS), and the sink also serves a page that lists every app's crashes. Declared on the server side in ac_cloud-c3-webserver (server/src/app.rs).
